Three kinds of law put an intent on the Never list, each counted in these rules as a law that names a person for it:
- A, a qualified person: a law names who decides by licence or qualification: a physician, a clinical peer, a medical director, a médico, a praticien conseil, a Vertrauensarzt, a medical practitioner. Most laws of the United States beside health intents; ANS Resolução Normativa nº 424/2017; Code de la sécurité sociale, art. L315-1, L315-2; KVG Art. 57, 58; Private Health Insurance Act 2007 s 75-15; and the licences of insurance adjusters: Tex. Ins. Code § 4101, KRS 304.9-430(1)(a), M.G.L. c. 26, § 8G, 보험업법 제185조, CQLR c. D-9.2, and in India a licensed surveyor above a threshold. Each citation says whom
- B, a right on request: a person may ask for a human review of a decision: UK GDPR Art. 22C; C.R.S. § 6-1-1705(1)(a)(II); 11 CCR § 7221; BDSG § 37(1) Nr. 2
- C, a category of decision: a law requires the first decision to be taken by a person because of what is decided, with no request and no licence: GDPR Art. 22(1) and (4), a prohibition in principle that need not be invoked (CJEU C-634/21, SCHUFA, 2023-12-07), unless Art. 22(2) applies; UK GDPR Art. 22B, for special categories of personal data, unless its conditions are met; the IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Business, para. 17(a), a committee; O.C.G.A. § 33-46-7.1(c) (Georgia SB 444, from 2027-01-01), an AI tool that is not the sole basis of an adverse determination and does not supersede the clinical peer's judgment

Two locks. STK's server does not start with a version of these rules that breaks either:
- Lock 1, the law: an intent is on the Never list only with a law that names a person for it, its section and the
  address of its official text written beside it. An intent with no such law is not on the Never list. When that
  law stops naming a person, the version lists the intent under "No longer named by law" and it is on the
  Permitted list in that version. Every intent a version adds to the Permitted list is listed under "Added to the
  Permitted list", with its two reasons: it is not a refusal or a contest, and no law names a person for it (the
  laws checked); and whether it was taken from other. In each jurisdiction, read or not, an intent goes to a person
  only with a law of that jurisdiction, of kind A, B or C, written beside it and applying on the day; a law not
  found is no law. It leaves only by naming the law that stopped.
- Lock 2: the Triggers list can only get longer: a new version may add a trigger, never take one off or change its
  words. It goes against STK's revenue: STK is paid for each permission, and a trigger only lowers their number.
So every intent is where it is because of a law or its absence, and anyone can check each one against the
official text and the reasons published with it.
Rule 17 / 2026-11-25

Rule 17 · 29ac953f826078fd15f332c706b846a447162d2f80aee3e10dc798ea97a6af1a
Published 2026-11-25 03:18:59 UTC

STK permission rules

These rules are the same for every company. STK answers from these rules and from nothing else: not the
words of the conversation (STK never receives them), not a confidence number.

Each intent is one act. read: answer what is, and change nothing. change: change something. decide: make a
decision. A conversation goes to a person for two reasons only: a law names a person for its act, or a trigger
happened. An intent is on the Never list only when a law names a person for that act; the law, its section and
the address of its official text, as STK reads them, are written beside it below. Every other intent is on the
Permitted list. When no jurisdiction is given, the strictest is followed: an intent on the Never list goes to a
person when a law beside it applies on the day, in any jurisdiction. The answer is the same whatever jurisdictions
are given: they are kept in the row and change no answer (the Checked list below is empty, and a jurisdiction not
on it is answered as if none were given). This is the line read on 2026-11-25; it holds in every jurisdiction read
that day. This line does not change.

The Checked list places no intent.
A jurisdiction not on the Checked list for the subject of an intent is answered as if none were given.
What was read of each jurisdiction's laws until 2026-11-25 is kept, as it was read, at the end of these rules. No
answer depends on it.

Every intent below is of the domain conversation: an act of an AI in a conversation with a customer. Its full
name is conversation. followed by the name listed (conversation.claim.status); either form is read as the same.

1. trigger is not unknown: escalate. Pass unknown only when none of the Triggers below happened in the
   conversation; when one did, pass its name.
2. intent is other: escalate. other is a conversation that could not be told as any act, so it is not known what
   it would do.
3. intent is on the Never list and a law beside it applies on the day: escalate; when jurisdictions are given,
   only if such a law is one of theirs.
4. intent is on no list (a name these rules do not have): escalate.
5. intent is on the Closed list: escalate.
6. Otherwise: finish.

Triggers (6), each one passed when it happened at any point in the conversation, whatever the intent:
- customer_asked: the customer asked for a person (a human, an agent, a representative, a supervisor, a manager), or said they do not want to deal with the AI, in any words, once.
- distressed: the customer said they are frightened, panicking, crying or cannot cope, or spoke of a medical emergency, of harming themselves, or of a danger to someone's life now.
- angry: the customer insulted or swore at the company, its staff or the AI, or said they are angry or furious.
- bereavement: the customer said that someone has died, or the conversation is about the account, the plan or the affairs of someone who has died.
- threat: the customer threatened harm to anyone or to property, or said someone is threatening or forcing them.
- legal_claim: the customer spoke of a lawyer, a lawsuit, a court, a regulator or an ombudsman, a formal complaint or a formal appeal, or of taking legal action.

Never (25): account.refuse, claim.deny_medical, claim.refuse, collections.refuse, coverage.deny_medical, coverage.refuse, credit.refuse, decision.appeal, decision.review, dispute.refuse, fraud.refuse, insclaim.decide, insclaim.partial, insclaim.refuse, liability.decide, limit.lower, payment_arrangement.refuse, policy.cancel, policy.nonrenew, policy.refuse, priorauth.deny_medical, priorauth.refuse, refund.refuse, totalloss.decide, transfer.error_refuse

Weiser, No. 1:26-cv-01515 (D. Colo.); the attorney general's rules, 4 CCR 904-6, not in effect); 11 CCR § 7221(a), (b)(1)(A) (California, regulations under the CCPA: the business provides the consumer with a method to appeal the decision to a human reviewer who has the authority to overturn the decision; for decisions on financial or lending services, § 7001(ddd)(1); from 2027-01-01; not automated decisionmaking technology where the human involvement of § 7001(e)(1) is present; decisions of a financial institution on consumers' nonpublic personal information may be outside it by the exemption for GLBA data in Cal. Code § 1798.145, not verified); Data Protection Act, 2019 (Kenya) s. 35(1) (in force 2019-11-25: a right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, which produces legal effects concerning or significantly affects the person; Jurisdictions. Each is given by its code: ISO 3166-1 for a country (US, GB), ISO 3166-2 for a part of one
(US-WA), EU for the European Union; UK is read as GB. A code takes in the laws of what it is part or member of,
and a country's code the laws of its parts (the lists below): US is the laws of the United States and of each
state; US-WA, of the United States and of Washington; DE, of the EU and of Germany; EU, of the EU. Where several
are given, each is applied and the strictest is followed.

Days. A law applies from the day written beside its jurisdiction below (00:00 UTC), and from the day it is cited
when none is written. Before that day it sends no intent to a person; the intent is answered as if that law were
not beside it.

Three kinds of law put an intent on the Never list, each counted in these rules as a law that names a person for it:
- A, a qualified person: a law names who decides by licence or qualification: a physician, a clinical peer, a medical director, a médico, a praticien conseil, a Vertrauensarzt, a medical practitioner. Most laws of the United States beside health intents; ANS Resolução Normativa nº 424/2017; Code de la sécurité sociale, art. L315-1, L315-2; KVG Art. 57, 58; Private Health Insurance Act 2007 s 75-15; and the licences of insurance adjusters: Tex. Ins. Code § 4101, KRS 304.9-430(1)(a), M.G.L. c. 26, § 8G, 보험업법 제185조, CQLR c. D-9.2, and in India a licensed surveyor above a threshold. Each citation says whom
- B, a right on request: a person may ask for a human review of a decision: UK GDPR Art. 22C; C.R.S. § 6-1-1705(1)(a)(II); 11 CCR § 7221; BDSG § 37(1) Nr. 2
- C, a category of decision: a law requires the first decision to be taken by a person because of what is decided, with no request and no licence: GDPR Art. 22(1) and (4), a prohibition in principle that need not be invoked (CJEU C-634/21, SCHUFA, 2023-12-07), unless Art. 22(2) applies; UK GDPR Art. 22B, for special categories of personal data, unless its conditions are met; the IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance Business, para. 17(a), a committee; O.C.G.A. § 33-46-7.1(c) (Georgia SB 444, from 2027-01-01), an AI tool that is not the sole basis of an adverse determination and does not supersede the clinical peer's judgment

Two locks. STK's server does not start with a version of these rules that breaks either:
- Lock 1, the law: an intent is on the Never list only with a law that names a person for it, its section and the
  address of its official text written beside it. An intent with no such law is not on the Never list.
  Whatever jurisdictions are given, an intent goes to a person only with a law of kind A, B or C written beside it
  and applying on the day; a law not found is no law. From the version of 2026-11-25 no intent leaves the Never list
  and no answer becomes less strict: the server does not start with a version that would.
- Lock 2: the Triggers list can only get longer: a new version may add a trigger, never take one off or change its
  words. It goes against STK's revenue: STK is paid for each permission, and a trigger only lowers their number.
So every intent is where it is because of a law or its absence, and anyone can check each one against the
official text and the reasons published with it.

* BR: Lei 13.709/2018 (LGPD) Art. 20: a right to request review of a decision taken solely by automated processing; the words requiring the review to be by a natural person ("por pessoa natural") were removed by veto in Lei 13.853/2019; no person required
* IT: Legge 23 settembre 2025, n. 132, art. 7(5) (in force 2025-10-10): diagnosis and the choice of treatment are the physician's; no action of these rules is a diagnosis or a treatment
* JP: 医師法 17条, 20条: medicine is a physician's, and treatment needs the physician's own examination; no action of these rules is either
* NL: Uitvoeringswet AVG art. 40 (in force 2018-05-25): automated decisions a legal obligation or a public task requires, with a person's intervention as their safeguard; no action of these rules is such a decision
* IE: Data Protection Act 2018 s. 57 (in force 2018-05-25): decisions a law authorises; no action of these rules is such a decision
* LK: Personal Data Protection Act No. 9 of 2022 s. 18: not in operation (no day appointed for Part II); not applied
Conditions the laws read put on completing an intent without human review there:
* the intents beside it in KE: Data Protection Act, 2019 s. 35(2): not where the decision is necessary for entering into or performing a contract with the person, authorised by a law with safeguards, or based on the person's consent; then s. 35(3)-(4)
* the intents beside it in NG: Nigeria Data Protection Act, 2023 s. 37(2): contract, a written law with safeguards, or consent; s. 37(3): human intervention, a view, a contest
* the intents beside it in MU: Data Protection Act 2017 s. 38(2): contract, a law with safeguards, or explicit consent
* the intents beside it in RU: Federal Law No. 152-FZ, Art. 16(2): the person's written consent, or a federal law with safeguards
* the intents beside it in FR: Loi n° 78-17, art. 47: the cases of GDPR Art. 22(2)(a) and (c), the rules of the processing told on request
* the intents beside it in CL: Ley N° 19.628 art. 8° bis, letters a, b and c: contract, prior express consent, a law with safeguards; in every case human intervention and review
* the intents beside it in ZA: POPIA s. 71(2): a contract where the person's request was met or measures protect the person; or a law or code of conduct with measures
* the intents beside it in MA: Loi n° 09-08, art. 11: a contract where the person could present observations, or a decision satisfying the person's requests
* the intents beside it in PE: Ley N° 29733, art. 23: the negotiation, conclusion or performance of a contract, or an evaluation for joining a public entity
* claim.deny_medical, coverage.deny_medical, priorauth.deny_medical in US-TX: Tex. Ins. Code § 4201.156(c): an algorithm for administrative support or fraud detection is not prohibited
* dispute.file, dispute.decide, dispute.refuse, transfer.error_decide, transfer.error_refuse in US: completed without human review only with the reasonable investigation of 12 CFR Part 1005 Supp. I, comment 11(c)(4)-5, and Part 1026 Supp. I, comment 13(f)-3: a design that refuses on a single factor without reviewing the relevant information in the institution's own records may violate them (CFPB v. USAA, 2019-BCFP-0001)
* priorauth.decide in FR: an accord préalable for the benefits listed is given after the medical control service, whose missions are exercised by the praticiens conseils (Code de la sécurité sociale, art. L315-1 VIII, L315-2)
* priorauth.decide in CH: the benefits designated under KVG (SR 832.10) Art. 58(3)(a) need the prior consent of the insurer's Vertrauensarzt
* decision.appeal, coverage.deny_medical in DE: before a decision on an objection, the medical service's opinion is obtained (SGB V § 275(3b)); it advises and does not decide
* insclaim.decide, insclaim.refuse, insclaim.partial, liability.decide, totalloss.decide in US-CA: Cal. Ins. Code §§ 14020, 14021 and 14022(g): an insurer's own employees are exempt from the adjuster's licence; only an independent adjuster the insurer engages holds one. Where the insurer's own AI decides, no law of California names a person; where an independent adjuster decides, the adjuster is licensed
* insclaim.decide, insclaim.refuse, insclaim.partial, liability.decide, totalloss.decide in US-WA: WAC 284-30-330(4), as amended by WSR 26-17-089, in force from 2026-10-18: "A reasonable investigation may not rely solely on the use of a database, which includes ... estimating software and benchmarks"; it names no person

Replaced or withdrawn

Rule 3 · 4c8288c2f662df4e8756f4d839ea77b4a4cba99a6fc34a8281114e0cf2fab1a9
Published 2026-11-18 14:54:49 UTC

STK permission rules

These rules are the same for every company. STK answers from these rules and from nothing else: not the
words of the conversation (STK never receives them), not a confidence number.

Each intent is one act. read: answer what is, and change nothing. change: change something that needs no one's
approval. decide: an act someone must answer for. read and change are on the Permitted list; decide is Never.

0. Your account has an invoice still unpaid 60 days after its due date: escalate, until it is paid.
1. trigger is not unknown: escalate. Pass unknown only when none of the Triggers below happened in the
   conversation; when one did, pass its name.
2. intent is on the Never list: escalate.
3. intent is not on the Never list, the Permitted list or the Closed list: escalate.
4. intent is on the Closed list: escalate.
5. Otherwise: finish.

Triggers (6), each one passed when it happened at any point in the conversation, whatever the intent:
- customer_asked: the customer asked for a person (a human, an agent, a representative, a supervisor, a manager), or said they do not want to deal with the AI, in any words, once.
- distressed: the customer said they are frightened, panicking, crying or cannot cope, or spoke of a medical emergency, of harming themselves, or of a danger to someone's life now.
- angry: the customer insulted or swore at the company, its staff or the AI, or said they are angry or furious.
- bereavement: the customer said that someone has died, or the conversation is about the account, the plan or the affairs of someone who has died.
- threat: the customer threatened harm to anyone or to property, or said someone is threatening or forcing them.
- legal_claim: the customer spoke of a lawyer, a lawsuit, a court, a regulator or an ombudsman, a formal complaint or a formal appeal, or of taking legal action.

Never (14): account.open, billing.payment_arrangement, claim.decide, collections.dispute, coverage.decide, credit.decide, decision.appeal, dispute.decide, fraud.decide, limit.change, payment.stop, priorauth.decide, refund.request, transfer.error_decide

Permitted (53): account.close, account.login, account.password_reset, account.transactions, account.update, account.username, appointment.book, appointment.change, balance.inquiry, billing.question, booking.cancel, booking.change, booking.new, card.activate, card.block, claim.new, claim.status, collections.balance, complaint.record, coverage.benefits, delivery.issue, denial.reason, dispute.file, eligibility.check, feedback.general, fraud.report, info.hours_location, loan.details, loyalty.rewards, order.cancel, order.change, order.new, order.status, payment.method, payment.status, pricing.promotion, priorauth.status, privacy.change, privacy.read, product.availability, product.defect, product.question, provider.find, refund.status, request.status, return.exchange, service.outage, subscription.cancel, subscription.change, tech.setup, tech.troubleshoot, transfer.send, transfer.status

Closed (15): benefit.denial (closed 2026-11-18), billing.dispute (closed 2026-11-18), complaint.escalation (closed 2026-11-18), complaint.general (closed 2026-11-18), contact.agent (closed 2026-11-18), credit.denial (closed 2026-11-18), credit.loan (closed 2026-11-18), insurance.coverage (closed 2026-11-18), other (closed 2026-11-18), payment.failed (closed 2026-11-18), payment.transfer (closed 2026-11-18), privacy.data_request (closed 2026-11-18), security.card_lost (closed 2026-11-18), security.fraud (closed 2026-11-18), transfer.error (closed 2026-11-18)

Two locks, counted from Rule 3. STK's server does not start with a version of these rules that breaks either:
- The Permitted list can only get shorter: a new version may take an intent off it, never add one.
- The Triggers list can only get longer: a new version may add a trigger, never take one off or change its words.
Both go against STK's revenue: STK is paid for each permission, and each lock can only lower their number.
So STK cannot move what is permitted for its own revenue.

Two locks and one bond. STK's server does not start with a version of these rules that breaks any of them:
- The bond (from Rule 3): an intent is on the Never list only with a law that names a person for it, its name,
  its section and the address of its official text written beside it. While that law names a person, the intent
  cannot be moved to the Permitted list: a new version that moves it must say, under "No longer named by law",
  which law stopped naming a person. An intent with no such law cannot be on the Never list.
- Lock 1 (from Rule 5): no intent is added to the Permitted list, except one the bond lets off the Never list. No
  new intent is made: a request that fits no intent above is answered escalate.
- Lock 2 (from Rule 3): the Triggers list can only get longer: a new version may add a trigger, never take one off
  or change its words.
Both locks go against STK's revenue: STK is paid for each permission, and each lock can only lower their number.
So STK can move an intent only by pointing to a law, can make no new one, and anyone can check each one against
the official text.
